title: Successor graph activation at predecessor epoch + 1
description:
Objective: close the one gap the graph supersession transition deliberately left open — a SUCCESSOR graph revision cannot currently activate at predecessor epoch + 1, so a superseded chain's second generation would re-activate at epoch 1 and the monotonic-epoch guarantee holds only for the emitted binding, never for the successor's own durable state.

Hard dependencies: Graph revision supersession transition (task-1df0622e87cf42beae2cd82280e9ff99). Nothing here is plannable until that task is DONE and `graphEpoch` exists on `GraphRevisionState` on disk.

*** MEASURED ON DISK 2026-08-09 at HEAD 025dc4948127e7c7b753b71d3f5cf4b142637060 by architect-8ee37119. Re-measure before planning; these claims are stale by default. ***

THE EPOCH AUTHORITY IS REAL AND ALREADY LANDED — do not mint a second one. The goal aggregate owns it exactly as `graph-revision-reducer.ts:5-7` claims:
- `goal-contract.ts:130,155` — `readonly graphEpoch: number` on goal state and on the activation event.
- `goal-reducer.ts:94` — `goal.create` seeds `graphEpoch: 0` on DRAFT.
- `goal-reducer.ts:110` — `goal.activate_initial_graph` sets `graphEpoch: state.graphEpoch + 1`.
- `goal-reducer.ts:113` — emits `GoalExecutionEnabled` CARRYING `graphEpoch`, so the wire that hands the epoch to a revision already exists.
- `goal-validation.ts:228-238` — validates it: safe integer, `>= 0`, DRAFT implies 0, COMPLETED implies > 0, active implies > 0.

THE ACTUAL GAP, both halves measured:
1. GOAL SIDE — `goal-reducer.ts:40` admits `goal.activate_initial_graph` from `DRAFT` ONLY. There is no command that advances a goal's `graphEpoch` a second time, so in practice the epoch can only ever be 0 or 1. Supersession needs an epoch advance admitted from the live execution lifecycle that increments `graphEpoch` and rebinds `activeGraphRevisionRef` to the successor revision.
2. GRAPH REVISION SIDE — the supersession transition task sets `graphEpoch: 1` literally when a revision activates (its DoD 1 says "initial activation establishes epoch 1"). A successor therefore cannot land at N+1. The activation path must instead bind the goal-issued epoch: it has to arrive on the command and be validated against the predecessor it replaces, not be hardcoded.

WHY IT WAS DEFERRED, not an oversight: DoD 2 of task-1df0622e requires only that the accepted supersede result EMIT a binding to the successor at exactly epoch + 1, which it does via the kernel-produced `GraphRevisionSuperseded` event. Making the successor's own activation consume that binding reaches `GraphActivationBinding`, `bindingShape`, `sameBinding`, `BINDING_KEYS`, the approval/activation fixtures and both invariant driver suites — far past the 10-file cap for that task.

SIZING WARNING, measured: `goal-reducer.ts` is 247 physical lines and `goal-validation.ts` is 245, both effectively at the 250 target with no headroom, so this work almost certainly requires splitting a file rather than growing one. Note also that `planning-source-size.test.ts` sweeps `src/planning` ONLY — `packages/core/src/goal/` is NOT guarded and `goal-reducer.test.ts` already sits at 300 lines. Do not read a green core suite as proof of the per-file cap in `goal/`; hand-measure with `grep -c ''`.

CONTAINED: `packages/core/src/planning/planning-contract.ts` does NOT share `GraphActivationBinding` — the planning-run aggregate carries its own hash set — so the planning-run reducer and its fixtures are outside this blast radius.

Likely owned paths (verify by fresh grep): packages/core/src/goal/goal-contract.ts, goal-reducer.ts, goal-validation.ts, goal-reducer.test.ts, goal-invariants.test.ts, packages/core/src/planning/graph-revision-contract.ts, graph-revision-validation.ts, graph-revision-reducer.ts, graph-revision-test-fixtures.ts, graph-revision-reducer.test.ts.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test
definitionOfDone: A goal-side epoch advance exists: a command admitted from the goal's live execution lifecycle (not only DRAFT) increments `graphEpoch` by exactly 1 and rebinds `activeGraphRevisionRef` to the named successor revision, composing the landed counter at goal-reducer.ts:110 rather than introducing a second epoch.

A graph revision activates at an epoch supplied by the goal aggregate instead of the literal 1: the activation path validates the incoming epoch against the predecessor it replaces, and an initial activation still lands at epoch 1 with every pre-active lifecycle at 0.

A successor revision produced by `graph.supersede` activates at exactly predecessor epoch + 1, proven end to end by a test that drives supersede then activates the successor and asserts the durable state epoch — not merely the emitted binding.

A stale, equal, skipped or non-integer epoch cannot activate a successor and cannot advance the goal; each refusal pins the exact stable @moe/contracts code and the refusing layer, and no parallel vocabulary is minted.

Every pre-existing assertion in goal-reducer.test.ts, goal-invariants.test.ts and graph-revision-reducer.test.ts passes unchanged except those the epoch binding genuinely invalidates, and a mutation drill proves each new epoch guard is reddenable.

Fresh `pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test` exits 0, and every touched production file is at or below 250 physical lines measured by `grep -c ''` — goal-reducer.ts (247) and goal-validation.ts (245) start with no headroom and will need splitting, not growing.
taskRails: Compose the landed goal epoch authority — goal-contract.ts:130/155, goal-reducer.ts:94/110/113, goal-validation.ts:228-238. Do not add a second epoch counter, and do not move epoch authority into the graph revision aggregate; that aggregate persists a BOUND REFERENCE to the epoch it was activated at, nothing more.

MEASURE BEFORE PLANNING: if the fresh grep shows this exceeds 10 distinct files or 12 plan steps, split at the goal/graph-revision seam rather than submitting an oversized plan — but a goal-side-only slice must name its consumer task, because a pure epoch advance with nothing binding it violates the composition clause.

packages/core/src/goal/ is NOT covered by planning-source-size.test.ts, so a green suite proves nothing about the per-file cap there. Hand-measure with `grep -c ''`; PowerShell Measure-Object -Line skips blank lines and reports headroom you do not have.

Refusal tests assert the exact stable reason code AND which layer refused, never merely that the operation failed. Note that @moe/contracts RuntimeError DROPS its validated `source`, so the layer must come from a production discriminant on the result — never from a test helper that reconstructs it.
An epoch that cannot be verified is UNKNOWN and refuses; it never defaults to 0, to 1, or to the predecessor's value.

ARCHITECT MEASUREMENT for the block, by architect-705f0380 at 19:06Z. Everything below measured at HEAD, not read from the description. Recording it in full here because report_blocked truncates, and because whoever unblocks this should not have to re-probe.

WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE (the description's "MEASURED ON DISK" claims all VERIFY):
- graphEpoch IS on GraphRevisionState: packages/core/src/planning/graph-revision-contract.ts:111 `readonly graphEpoch: number`. Committed at HEAD, confirmed with git show.
- graph.supersede is NO LONGER routed to illegal. graph-revision-reducer.ts:69 lists it, :78 admits it from ACTIVE, :200 routes `case "graph.supersede": return supersede(state, command)`. Committed at HEAD. architect-8ee37119 measured this as an open gap earlier today; that half is closed.
- The goal-side epoch authority is exactly where the description says: goal-contract.ts:130 and :155 carry graphEpoch; goal-reducer.ts:94 seeds 0 on DRAFT, :110 sets state.graphEpoch + 1, :113 emits GoalExecutionEnabled carrying it, :175 reseeds 0 on the new goal. Do NOT mint a second counter.
- Working tree is CLEAN against HEAD over packages/core/src/planning/graph-revision-*.ts and packages/core/src/goal/*.ts.

WHY IT IS STILL BLOCKED, and it is not the missing symbol:
The stated hard dependency task-1df0622e87cf42beae2cd82280e9ff99 (Graph revision supersession transition) is WORKING with an 11-step plan, NOT DONE. This task's own description is unambiguous: "Nothing here is plannable until that task is DONE and graphEpoch exists on GraphRevisionState on disk." Half of that condition is met; the other half is not.

The concrete hazard is a collision, not a missing surface. mtimes, offset-corrected (host prints +0300, board is UTC):
  graph-revision-reducer.ts   2026-08-09 21:55:40 +0300  =  18:55:40Z  -- ELEVEN MINUTES before I measured
  graph-revision-contract.ts  2026-08-09 21:44:41 +0300  =  18:44:41Z
Clean-versus-HEAD plus a fresh mtime means that worker is editing AND committing as they go, so these bytes are moving, not settled.

THE OVERLAP IS EXACT, NOT INCIDENTAL. This task's DoD 2 requires replacing the literal `graphEpoch: 1` in the activation path with a goal-issued epoch validated against the predecessor. That literal lives in the activation path of graph-revision-reducer.ts — the same file task-1df0622e is mutating right now, and its DoD 1 is what put the literal there ("initial activation establishes epoch 1"). Two plans rewriting one activation path in a shared worktree is the collision epic rail 3 exists to prevent, and the loser silently loses bytes. Any line number I pinned now would be stale before a worker read it.

WHAT UNBLOCKS THIS, precisely:
1. task-1df0622e reaches DONE and its bytes are committed.
2. Re-measure the activation path in graph-revision-reducer.ts and confirm where the epoch literal actually ended up — it may not be line-stable or even literal by then.
Then this is plannable immediately; the goal-side half needs no waiting at all.

DoD 6 requires touched production files at or below 250, so this work requires SPLITTING a file, not growing one. packages/core/src/goal/ is NOT covered by planning-source-size.test.ts, so a green suite proves nothing about the cap there — hand-measure.

A SPLIT IS AVAILABLE IF THE BOARD WANTS PARALLELISM: the goal-side epoch advance (DoD 1) touches only packages/core/src/goal/ and does not overlap task-1df0622e at all. It could be planned and landed now. But taskRail 2 requires a goal-side-only slice to name its consumer, because a pure epoch advance with nothing binding it violates the composition clause — the consumer would be this task's graph-revision half. That is a governor call, not mine to make unilaterally.
